# Defect register

**Generated by `npm run defects` — do not hand-edit.** Every row is derived from a
`finding.raised` / `finding.ruled` pair in [`team-log/events.jsonl`](team-log/events.jsonl).
A defect that is not in the log is not in this file, which is the point: the register cannot
drift from the record, and `npm run log:audit` reconciles the record against git.

> **What is here.** Anything crossing a role boundary — one role's finding about another's
> work or about the design — including a role's finding against its own earlier work. A role's
> in-flight self-correction is *not* a defect; recording those would make a careful role look
> worse than a careless one.
>
> **Rejected findings stay, with their ruling.** A finding argued down on reasoning is evidence
> the adjudication worked. The most valuable finding in slice 00a was one whose measurement was
> right and whose proposed remedy would have broken the following slice — `narrowed` exists for
> exactly that, because the finding and the remedy are separate verdicts.

| Raised by | test-engineer 10 · implementer 9 · architect 3 · orchestrator 2 |
| Awaiting a ruling | none |
| Mean escape distance | 1.21 step(s) |

*Escape distance is the number of loop steps between where a defect entered and where it was
caught. Zero means it was caught in the step that produced it. It is the shift-left measure
`team-log/process-criteria.md` names, and it is only computable because findings are logged
rather than narrated.*

<details><summary>Failure scenarios and rulings</summary>

**O1** — The AC-4 fixture and lint:arch can both pass while examining nothing

- *scenario:* Built the fixture to spec with four planted violations: depcruise exited 0, reported 0 violations, cruised 0 modules, because no typescript was resolvable. The negative control passes vacuously and lint:arch would report a clean architecture over an unexamined tree, so C4 reads a false green.
- *file:* `docs/slices/00a-design.md`
- *narrowed* by architect — Finding upheld as (c). Remedy tightened: "resolves the real compiler" is not a mechanism, and totalCruised > 0 is the weak form — every planted file must appear in modules[].

**O2** — No acceptance test can start the service — no entrypoint, no loader, no owner

- *scenario:* AC-1 and AC-2 both require a running service. The design names no start script, typecheck is --noEmit so nothing is emitted, tests/support/ has no owner and package.json scripts are unassigned.
- *file:* `docs/slices/00a-design.md`
- *narrowed* by architect — Finding upheld as (a). Remedy rejected: no TypeScript loader — tsx is in no ADR and --experimental-strip-types does not remap .js specifiers. The project compiles instead, so the acceptance test spawns the artifact a deployment would run.

**O3** — The reasoning for implementer-authored tool tests is factually wrong

- *scenario:* test:tools is a literal && chain of named files, not a glob, so a new tools/test/*.test.mjs does not run in CI until wired. Test-engineer-authored tool tests can therefore be red and invisible to verify, which also makes evidence item 3 independently authored.
- *file:* `docs/slices/00a-design.md`
- *accepted* by architect — Conceded outright: the stated reason was false and the conclusion does not survive it.

**O-1** — red-proof's red zone makes slices 07 and 11 structurally unable to pass

- *scenario:* The rule requires a failing file under tests/acceptance/. Slice 07 has only tests/concurrency/ and slice 11 only tests/performance/, so a correctly red commit exits 1. The negative condition is also stricter than AC-6, which constrains what must pass.
- *file:* `docs/slices/00a-design.md`
- *escalated* by human — Finding upheld; the proposed remedy was REJECTED in part — excluding tests/integration/ would break slice 00, whose only test file lives there. Reading of AC-6 escalated to the human, who ruled BROAD: any test-engineer-owned suite.

**O-2** — collect-ci's three constraints are correct but not sufficient

- *scenario:* check.mjs:113 reads runs.at(-1) positionally while gh returns newest-first, so tests-green is judged on a stale run; and schema.mjs defaults ts to collection time, so collecting a red and a green run together makes C1 report FAIL on a correctly test-first slice.
- *file:* `docs/slices/00a-design.md`
- *accepted* by architect — Both agreed as constraints 4 and 5. The deeper fix to check.mjs declined: changing the gate tool in the slice that first feeds it is how you get a gate that agrees with its own bug.

**S-1** — The design worked around a NON-NEGOTIABLE and called it a bootstrap paradox

- *scenario:* CLAUDE.md §2.4 requires the red observed in CI; §7 offered four substitutes instead. METHODOLOGY:272 bars the board from leaving red until CI records the failure and :335 defines step 3 as logging that run, so the design produced an unloggable state, not merely weaker evidence.
- *file:* `docs/slices/00a-design.md`
- *accepted* by architect — Self-raised and self-ruled (c) on §2 authority. Fixed by landing the suite CI job in the red commit. Exposed a gap in §6 — the (c) test could not name a §2 invariant — since corrected in all three places the rule is stated.

**F1** — §7's predicted reason for AC-3's red is falsified by §4's own mkdirSync

- *scenario:* globalSetup creates src/persistence/migrations before any test runs, so depcruise can open src and exits 0 over 18 modules. Two mechanisms specified in separate sections cancel each other.
- *file:* `docs/slices/00a-design.md`
- *accepted* by architect — Agreed; §4 and §7 both carried a false mechanism. The test-engineer's coverage assertion stands and is better than either mechanism.

**F2** — The lint:arch guard cannot detect an unexamined src/ — O1's failure mode inside O1's own remedy

- *scenario:* The guard exits non-zero if no modules were cruised, but lint:arch cruises src tests and tests/ alone holds the count above zero. src/ goes unexamined behind a green gate and C4 reads a clean architecture.
- *file:* `docs/slices/00a-design.md`
- *narrowed* by architect — Finding agreed; remedy refined — roots derived from argv, not hardcoded, and a single cruise, because outside-in-tests-do-not-import-src only fires when both roots share a graph. Prompted the general rule now in §5.

**F4** — The typescript pin is load-bearing and nothing warns if it is broken

- *scenario:* npm i -D typescript installs 7.0.2; dependency-cruiser@18.2.0 supports >=2.0.0 <7.0.0 in src/meta.cjs, not peerDependencies, so there is no npm warning of any kind. Every cruise becomes inert and QS-10 switches off silently.
- *file:* `package.json`
- *accepted* by architect — Agreed and made worse on the architect’s own check: the range is internal, so nothing warns at install time. Pin marked exact with the citation.

**F6** — collect-ci exports one mapper where constraint 4 needs a list-level export

- *scenario:* Ascending order is a property of a list; with only toCheckRunRecord the ordering would live in the unexercised CLI and no test could reach it.
- *file:* `docs/slices/00a-design.md`
- *accepted* by architect — Agreed. Division of labour stated: per-run shape and ts in the singular, ordering in the plural, I/O and idempotence in the CLI.

**F7** — engines.node promises support the dependency tree refuses

- *scenario:* The declared >=22.11.0 <25 admits 22.11, which vitest and testcontainers both reject, and 23.x, which vitest and dependency-cruiser both reject. CI is unaffected, so the only person who hits it is a developer the repository told was supported.
- *file:* `package.json`
- *accepted* by architect — Agreed and found wrong twice rather than once. Corrected to >=22.22.0 <23 \|\| >=24.0.0 <25; the numbers are the architect’s per arc42 §7.1, not TC-10’s.

**I-1** — npm run typecheck is red at HEAD in a file the implementer may not edit

- *scenario:* A false as ChildProcessWithoutNullStreams assertion; stdio ignore makes stdin null. Vitest transpiles without typechecking so the red commit never saw it, and green commit 9 puts typecheck on the verify job.
- *file:* `tests/support/service.ts`
- *accepted* by test-engineer — Fixed by declaring the overload’s real type. Emitted JS diffed identical, so the step-3 failure diagnosis is unchanged. Exposed that tsconfig.build.json excludes tests/, so pretest only looked like it typechecked the harness.

**I-3** — §10's four-module prediction for graph:modules does not hold literally

- *scenario:* mermaid output ignores reporterOptions.archi.collapsePattern, so the render is per-file inside directory subgraphs plus every node_modules package.
- *file:* `docs/slices/00a-design.md`
- *accepted* by architect — Agreed, cosmetic, gates nothing; recorded alongside the existing note that this render is to be eyeballed rather than trusted.

**J-1** — judgeCruiseResult(summary, roots) cannot express the per-root rule it was ruled to enforce

- *scenario:* Coverage needs modules[], a sibling of summary; a summary carries only totalCruised. And lint-arch.test.mjs passed bare summaries, so every committed case judged the F2 rule vacuously.
- *file:* `docs/slices/00a-design.md`
- *narrowed* by architect — Finding agreed; remedy narrowed — a bare summary stays legitimate because three of four rules read only it, roots stays optional, and a missing modules[] gets its own distinct verdict.

**J-2** — Repo-relative normalisation breaks the offline replay it exists to enable

- *scenario:* Vitest records the runner’s absolute paths, so relative(cwd, name) yields ../../../home/runner/... matching neither the red zone nor the must-pass set. A genuinely red run replays as "no suite failed" — the discriminator reporting the opposite of what happened, on the one path that checks it.
- *file:* `tools/ci/red-proof.mjs`
- *accepted* by architect — Agreed; last-/tests/-segment fallback adopted and stated as a precondition of evidence item 3. Both alternatives recorded as rejected.

**J-3** — gh exposes job display names, not workflow keys

- *scenario:* The REST API does not expose the YAML key, so jobs.verify needs a name-to-key map; unmapped names must be slugified rather than dropped, or a failing job is invisible to constraint 2.
- *file:* `tools/team-log/collect-ci.mjs`
- *accepted* by architect — Agreed with two additions: a conformance assertion tying JOB_KEYS to verify.yml, and not-run failing closed against check.mjs:128.

**A-1** — The layering guard can run the analyser it exists to guard against

- *scenario:* The PATH fallback sits two lines below its own comment forbidding it. A global depcruise has its own node_modules and its own typescript resolution — the different-analyser scenario, minus the network.
- *file:* `tools/ci/lint-arch.mjs`
- *accepted* by architect — Self-raised. Fallback becomes exit 2 naming npm ci as the fix, which makes the comment true.

**T-1** — An assertion no correct collector could satisfy, unnoticed because the file was unwired

- *scenario:* The green-then-red case fed the same two records in reversed array order, but check.mjs finds the failing run by regex and orders by timestamp, so array order cannot change the verdict. 29 of 30 passed and nothing ran the 30th.
- *file:* `tools/test/collect-ci.test.mjs`
- *accepted* by test-engineer — Self-raised and fixed using the captured pre-slice green run rather than a third derived fixture. Produced the four-point discipline now applied to every assertion.

**T-2** — repoRelative is not tested at all, and its fixtures encode a false belief about the tool

- *scenario:* red-proof.test.mjs never imports failedFilesFrom, and its fixtures resolve against the local cwd so relative() always answers and the second branch never runs. §6 requires fixtures captured from the tool rather than encoding a belief about it; that was honoured for the gh payloads and not for the Vitest JSON.
- *file:* `tools/test/red-proof.test.mjs`
- *accepted* by test-engineer — Agreed and worse than stated. The red run’s real artifact is now a committed fixture; a relative()-only reader is shown to report "nothing failed" on the run that failed twice.

**I-7** — Most of two CLIs carry rules that survive their own deletion with no test failing

- *scenario:* lint-arch.mjs deliberately discards depcruise’s exit code because --output-type json exits 0 with violations present. Revert that and lint:arch goes green on every violation with nothing failing — the mutant prints the violation and exits 0.
- *file:* `tools/ci/lint-arch.mjs`
- *accepted* by test-engineer — Self-raised by the implementer when asked. All four named rules pinned, each watched failing against its mutant.

**T-3** — The compiler diagnosis reports no compiler when one is installed

- *scenario:* Three version reads shared one try, and dependency-cruiser’s exports map hides package.json, so a failure to read its version asserted that typescript was missing. It fires exactly when a developer has a working toolchain and a real violation.
- *file:* `tools/ci/lint-arch.mjs`
- *accepted* by implementer — Fixed by resolving package entry points and walking to the manifest, with per-fact failure isolation so a partial read yields a shorter true line.

**O-3** — log:audit reports 12 false discrepancies because it assumes one agent.finish per transcript

- *scenario:* A resumed agent stops once per resume, writing one agent.finish each, but all resumes share a single subagent transcript. The audit pairs records to transcripts one-to-one, so it reports UNSUPPORTED for every resume after the first and MISMATCH on duration because the transcript spans all of them. Slice 00a resumed the architect six times, so the audit now reports the honest record as untrustworthy — which is worse than not auditing, because C7 reads this output.
- *file:* `tools/team-log/audit.mjs`
- *deferred* by orchestrator — Real and mine, but out of scope for slice 00a: audit.mjs is orchestrator tooling and the fix is not a slice deliverable. Recorded rather than silently tolerated, because an audit that cries wolf twelve times is one nobody reads. Same root cause as the report-capture overwrite fixed in bdb32c1 — both tools were written assuming one spawn equals one run, and SendMessage resumes break that. Carried to the phase-4 retro under C7.

**O-4** — The unit tests are far weaker than a green suite suggests: mutation score 0.0634 against a Definition-of-Done threshold of 0.75

- *scenario:* Stryker, installed at step 5 having been required by CLAUDE.md section 3 and section 10 since the constitution was written, reports 9 killed and 130 survived of 142 mutants over 43 unit tests. Four of seven source files kill nothing at all, including checkHealth.ts and persistence/db.ts which have dedicated unit test files. 24 BlockStatement mutants survive, meaning 24 places where an entire block can be replaced with an empty one and no test notices; 19 ConditionalExpression mutants survive, meaning branch conditions can be forced either way unobserved. Verified real rather than a configuration artifact by inspecting a survivor directly.
- *file:* `tests/unit/`
- *accepted* by human — Ruled by the human at step 4: strengthen the unit tests rather than relax the threshold or defer it as debt. The alternatives considered and rejected were ruling the 0.75 threshold not-applicable to a walking skeleton, which would be a Definition-of-Done change, and accepting the score as a recorded debt with a follow-up slice. The survivors are genuine weaknesses and finding them is why mutation testing is in the stack, so the work is the implementer own in tests/unit/.

**O-5** — The 0.0634 mutation score ruled BLOCKING was a harness artifact, not a measurement of the tests

- *scenario:* stryker-mutator/vitest-runner 10.0.0 does not activate mutants under vitest 5.0.0. Its peer range is vitest >=2.0.0, so npm warns about nothing. 118 of the 130 reported survivors carried testsCompleted 0 — Stryker ran no test against them and recorded them as survived. Only 21 of 142 mutants were tested at all. Decisive check: checkHealth.ts scored 0 of 6 against a file with six dedicated tests, and activating one of those mutants by hand in Stryker own unmodified sandbox with STRYKER_ACTIVE_MUTANT set killed it via 5 existing failing tests. The true baseline was 76.06, not 6.34. Same shape as dependency-cruiser typescript range: a tool reporting a number over work it never did, with nothing warning.
- *file:* `stryker.config.mjs`
- *accepted* by orchestrator — Correct, verified independently, and it is a finding against the orchestrator. I provisioned Stryker, watched it instrument 142 mutants and emit a score, and treated that score as a measurement without checking that any mutant had been activated — while writing a commit message about not working around missing tools. The sixth instance of this slice own rule and the first one I committed myself: a cruise that exits 0 says nothing about what it examined, and a mutation score says nothing about tests that were never run. The switch to the command runner is accepted; the implementer flagged the edit to a file it does not own rather than slipping it in. The underlying finding stands regardless of the bad number: the work was ruled on a false 6.34, but the true 76.06 was still below the 0.75 gate only marginally, and four of the individual weaknesses it found were real.

</details>

*A finding is recorded with `npm run log:append`; the orchestrator alone writes the log
(`CLAUDE.md` §9). Regenerate with `npm run defects`; CI checks it with `npm run defects:check`.*
